messages:
devon: Heads-up: canary perf spike after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (prob commit abc1f9). Seeing ~12% p50 regression on our long-seq workload. nsys snapshot attached, but short summary below.

maria: ugh, timeline? quick numbers pls (p50/p95/delta).

devon: p50 went from 48ms -> 54ms, p95 120ms -> 132ms. token throughput down ~8%. KV cache miss rate jumped: 4% -> 11% on canary logs.

sam: did kernel choice change for long sequences only? which kernel variant was chosen more often?

devon: yep — selector started preferring kernel_v2_small_tiles for long seqs after the new score function. nsys flame shows long memcpy+kernel_v2_small_tiles at same interval. snippet:
```
nsys stats: GPU time 1.8s, memcpyHtoD 120ms, kernel_v2_small_tiles 1.1s, kv_read_kernel 300ms
flame top: memcpy -> kernel_v2_small_tiles -> io_wait
```

li: small_tiles does more mem copies per tile, so expected to blow up on long seqs. our old kernel_big_tile had fewer launches.

maria: can you paste the selector decision trace? we log selector.reason right?

devon: pasted below from canary logs (simplified):
```
[selector] seq_len=2048 -> score_small=0.78 score_big=0.62 -> choose small_tiles commit=abc1f9
[cache] key_latency=1.8ms miss=false
[cache] miss_rate_window=0.11
```

sam: interesting that cache miss rate rose. could be more concurrent worker churn causing evictions when small_tiles increases memory traffic.

perf-bot: ci/profiler/canary-3612345678: nsys report: https://ci.redwood/profiler/3612345678 (summary attached).

ci-bot: bisect started: git bisect run -- cmd ./run_canary_profile.sh --profile nsight --warmup 100 --iters 500

maria: do a quick bisect locally if possible. try to confirm first bad commit.

devon: ran bisect overnight; first bad commit: abc1f9 (author: tanya) — matches the selector rewrite.

sam: can we repro with a focused micro-benchmark? one request pattern long seq + repeated KV hits.

devon: yes repro script: ./bench/long_seq_kv.sh --seq 2048 --qps 100. repro shows same p50 regression.

li: quick mitigation options:
- revert selector change (fast)
- tweak score function to bias big_tile when seq_len>1024
- increase KV cache size / TTL to reduce eviction noise

maria: I prefer tweak first to avoid full revert. can we test score tweak on canary?

devon: pushed quick patch that hard-codes fallback to big_tile for seq_len>=1536 to a canary branch. nsys diff looks promising: memcpy down 75ms, kernel_v2_small_tiles time drops 800ms.

sam: nice. did throughput recover?

devon: p50 back to 49ms in canary, p95 124ms. KV miss rate down to 5%. still monitoring.

maria: next: create PR with selector unit tests and add perf regression check in CI for this workload. also add a small perf test that asserts no >5% p50 regression on long_seq baseline.

perf-bot: TODO created: PERF-issue-1843 (regression check + test).

li: one more ask — add a short NVTX span in selector decision path so next nsys capture makes mapping trivial.

devon: will add NVTX and a perfnote in PR. plan: land tweak, run full e2e, then prepare revert PR if anything else pops.

maria: thanks, team. keep thread updated if canary diverges. :thumbsup:
